fields.home.title: A Letter for Ain
fields.home.dedication: Words from my heart to yours
fields.home.credit: Written by Muhammad Afif Aiman for Nur Ain Syazwani
fields.letter.cover.title: My Confession to You
fields.letter.cover.dedication: To Ain, who holds the key to my heart
fields.letter.intro.title: A Few Words First
fields.letter.intro.body: Hello, it's Afif here. Let me share something with you. My full name is Muhammad Afif Aiman. For now, that's what matters most. I know this may seem unusual, but I wanted to create something genuine. Something that comes from the heart. Making things for someone special feels more meaningful than anything else. That's all I wanted to say for now. Let's continue...
fields.letter.question.title: The Question
fields.letter.question.lead: Here we are. You know why I made this. It's a confession from me to you.
fields.letter.question.ask: Will you walk this journey with me?
fields.letter.next.title: What Comes Next
fields.letter.next.body: And here we are. You said yes! I know this might feel a bit unexpected, but sometimes the best moments come from surprises. I don't have long speeches prepared, but I truly hope this journey brings out the best in both of us. We can learn from each other, grow together, and build something meaningful. The next page contains a poem I wrote specially for you. I hope you like it.
fields.letter.poem.title: Our First Chapter
letter.poem.stanzas: I haven't discovered all of you yet,
and perhaps that's what makes this beautiful.
not someone I'm trying to fix —
I won't claim to be flawless,
or that I'll get everything right.
I'm not here out of routine.
I'm here because I picked you.
with nothing from the past weighing us down.
fields.letter.quotes.title: Words from My Heart
fields.letter.quotes.lead: These lines capture what I feel for you – honest thoughts from deep within.
fields.book.title: Verses for You
fields.book.dedication:
To Nur Ain Syazwani —
these lines belong to you.
fields.book.note: You reminded me why words matter.
fields.apology.title: I'm Sorry
fields.apology.intro:
This part is harder to write than the rest. Not every page can be about the good moments — some have to be about the times I let you down.

So here it is, plainly, without dressing it up: I'm sorry. These are the words I owe you.
fields.apology.closing: If you're still reading this far, thank you for giving me the chance to say it.

poems.title: The Sudden Shift
stanzas: It’s strange how quickly a story line can bend,
How a simple contact name stops being “just a friend.”
Yesterday you were just another thought passing through my head,
Now your morning message is the very first thing I read.
There were no dramatic movie scenes, no light up in the sky,
Just a sudden realization of how fast the hours fly
Whenever you’re around, or when your name pops on my screen,
Flipping every single ordinary moment in between.
I used to move through daily routines without a second thought,
Now I'm tangled up in every little moment that you caught.
It’s a brand new baseline, a total shift in how I view my day,
And honestly, I wouldn't have it any other way.

poems.title: Early Days & Car Park Conversations
stanzas: We’re still figuring out the exact mechanics of how this fits,
Navigating the quiet moments and the awkward little bits.
Learning which of my dumb jokes land and which ones hit the wall,
Trying to figure out the right time for a late-night call.
Sitting parked in the car for hours after driving you back home,
Talking about absolute nonsense, neither reaching for a phone.
The engine's turned off, the dashboard lights are fading low,
And neither one of us is in a hurry to get up and go.
It’s unwritten, it’s brand new, it’s slightly clumsy at the start,
But watching it unfold is the most exciting part.
We’re building a foundation out of simple, quiet nights,
Just two people getting it right beneath the streetlights.

poems.title: Overthinking the Unsent Text
stanzas: I catch myself overthinking every single thing I send,
Typing out a paragraph, erasing it, changing the end.
Trying so hard to play it cool and keep a steady pace,
While secretly just counting down the hours till I see your face.
Do I send a double text or wait for you to reply?
Why am I acting like a amateur, over-analyzing why?
It’s hilarious, it’s exhausting, but it’s real as it can be—
This ridiculous, amazing phase of letting someone in to see.
I drop the cool facade the second your message lights up bright,
Realizing all that overthinking wasn't worth the fight.
It's just us figuring it out, one draft at a time,
Finding the balance in this brand new rhythm and rhyme.

poems.title: The Notification High
stanzas: My phone lies on the desk, face down while I try to work,
Every minor vibration turns me into a watchful jerk.
I glance over immediately, hoping it’s your name appearing,
Cutting through the busy noise and everything I’m hearing.
It’s crazy how a simple three-word line sent on the fly
Can completely change my mood and raise my spirits high.
A random photo of your lunch, a quick meme out of nowhere,
Just a subtle little reminder that you’re sitting over there.
It brightens up the heavy hours, turns the grey into clear blue,
Proving how easily my whole day turns around because of you.
Not over-the-top, just a steady, subtle little spark,
A tiny little lantern cutting straight through the dark.

poems.title: Small Talks & Unfiltered Hours
stanzas: We spend hours talking about nothing—our days, our food,
The silly little random things that put us in a mood.
We don’t need deep philosophical debates or poetic prose,
It’s just easy, unscripted, and that’s how the evening goes.
I don’t have to keep up a performance or put on a show,
I can just sit back, relax, and let the real version show.
Messy hair, tired eyes, and stories from work that drag on long,
Yet with you listening on the line, nothing feels out of song.
We’re stripping away the polished surface people usually display,
Finding comfort in the casual things we choose to say.
Building something genuine out of everyday background noise,
Finding our natural cadence, finding our shared voice.

poems.title: The Butterfly Phase
stanzas: That sudden, nervous flutter right before we’re set to meet,
Walking side by side down an ordinary, crowded street.
My hands are in my pockets, wondering if I should reach out,
Hoping I’m making sense, hoping I don’t give you reason to doubt.
Every time our shoulders bump, my brain goes momentarily blank,
Forgetting what I was saying, losing track of my own bank
Of thoughts and clever lines I spent all afternoon preparing,
Replaced by the sheer distraction of the glance that you’re sharing.
It’s the butterfly phase—clumsy, raw, and slightly out of control,
The kind of good nervousness that takes over your entire soul.
A little bit chaotic, but the sweetest kind of rush,
Hiding a ridiculous grin behind a sudden, simple blush.

poems.title: Inside Jokes & Coded Language
stanzas: We’ve already started building our own private little language,
A collection of weird references that only we can manage.
A quick side-eye across a room full of people we know,
Communicating entire sentences without making a show.
An old joke from three days ago that makes no sense to anyone else,
Stored away like little treasures kept high up on the shelf.
It’s early in the game, but the vault is filling fast
With memories and funny moments made to actually last.
When standard words fall short, an inside joke steps in,
Rewinding back to that moment with a subtle, knowing grin.
It’s our own tiny world tucked inside the bigger one outside,
Where every little glance becomes a secret place to hide.

poems.title: My Favorite Distraction
stanzas: I’m supposed to be focused, I’ve got a long task list today,
But my mind keeps taking detours and wandering your way.
I stare at a blank screen, replaying how you laughed last night,
Remembering the way your hair looked in the dim restaurant light.
Work can wait a few extra minutes while I relive the conversation,
Lost entirely in this brand new, wonderful distraction.
You’ve officially taken over the background of my mind,
Pushing all the stressful, boring worries far behind.
I try to pull myself together and act like I'm locked in,
Then your text comes through and the distraction starts again.
And honestly? I wouldn't trade this lack of focus for the world,
Watching this new dynamic slowly get unfurled.

poems.title: Sanctuary in the Noise
stanzas: The rest of the world moves fast, demanding way too much,
Constantly rushing around, out of tune and out of touch.
But stepping into our space feels like hitting a total pause,
Escaping all the daily stress, the expectations, and the laws.
With you, there’s no pressure to be impressive or act grand,
Just sitting side by side, enjoying where we land.
A safe haven built without a single brick or wooden beam,
Much more grounded and reliable than any distant dream.
When the day gets heavy and the noise begins to rise,
I find an instant sense of quiet looking in your eyes.
It’s a brand new sanctuary, simple, quiet, and clear,
Where all the outside clutter just seems to disappear.

poems.title: Taking It Day by Day
stanzas: We don't need to overthink where this goes down the line,
Or try to map out future years like some master design.
We don’t have to rush the steps or stress about what’s next,
Analyzing every milestone like a complicated text.
Let’s just take it day by day, enjoying where we are right now,
Appreciating how we got here without worrying about how
The future holds its pieces, or what tomorrow has to bring,
As long as we keep enjoying the simple, present thing.
Here’s to the nervous beginnings, the awkward moments and the grace,
Taking every single step together at our own steady pace.
Just two people starting out, hands intertwined and free,
Excited for the next chapter of whatever this will be.

apologyPoems.title: Where I Fell Short
stanzas: There were days you needed more than I knew how to give,
A calmer kind of patience, a gentler way to live.
I answered you too slowly, I noticed things too late,
And let the little silences grow heavy with their weight.
I told myself you'd understand, that there was always time,
That love could fill the empty space between each careless line.
But love is in the showing up, not only in the word,
And I'm sorry for the moments when you felt unheard.
You never asked for perfect, you only asked for true,
For someone who would notice all the quiet things you do.
And if I missed them, even once, I need you to know:
It wasn't that I didn't care — I just learned too slow.

apologyPoems.title: Not Enough
stanzas: Some nights I lie awake and count the ways I've fallen short,
The moments I was distant when you needed my support.
You deserve someone steady, someone certain, someone whole,
And I'm still only learning how to give you all my soul.
I'm not the finished version of the man I want to be,
I'm rough around the edges, still unsure of half of me.
But every flaw I carry, I can see it clearer now,
And seeing is the first step — I'm still learning how.
So if I wasn't enough for you on days you needed more,
I'm sorry that you had to knock on such a heavy door.
I'm not asking you to settle, or to wait on me forever,
Just let me show you I can grow — and grow with you, together.

apologyPoems.title: What I Can Promise
stanzas: I can't promise I won't stumble, I can't promise I won't fall,
I can't promise every answer or the perfect words at all.
But I can promise honesty, and effort every day,
And when I'm wrong, I'll own it, not just hope it goes away.
I'll listen when you're quiet, I'll ask instead of guess,
I'll show up on the ordinary days, not just the best.
I'll learn the way you need to be loved, not the way I planned,
And hold on to you gently, with a softer, steadier hand.
You were never too much, Ain — I just wasn't yet enough,
But I'm staying, and I'm growing, even when it's rough.
So here's my heart, a little bruised, but honest, and still true:
I'm sorry. And I'm trying. And I'm still choosing you.

heart: "You mean the world to me, beyond what words can describe."
"My heart made its choice. I offer you my sincere love."
"You bring light to my every day. I belong to you."
"When I'm with you, I've found my comfort. My love for you has no end."
"Time spent with you is precious. You carry my heart."
"I admit it: without you, something feels missing."
"You're everything I ever wanted. My love stretches to infinity."
"My soul found its match. This is my vow to you."
"Each day I fall for you more. You are my joy."
"Our story begins here. I love you, now and always."
others: "The best thing to hold onto in life is each other." — Audrey Hepburn
"You are my sun, my moon, and all my stars." — E.E. Cummings
"In all the world, there is no love for you like mine." — Maya Angelou
"I love you not only for what you are, but for what I am when I am with you." — Roy Croft
